title: Version Control
equation: History Value = Σ Size of Each Tracked Change
hook: You changed your pricing three times this year and can't remember which version actually worked.
statement: Keep a record of every major change so you can see what actually worked.
explainer: If you don't track changes, you lose the ability to compare. This seems better turns into a guess. A simple changelog turns it into something you can actually learn from.
sop: Date every big change to a plan, price, process, or strategy.
Write down what changed, why, and what you expected to happen.
Score the size of each change from 1 to 10.
Roll back to the old version if the new one underperforms.
Review the log every quarter to see what really worked.
equation_example: Change 1 was a 3, Change 2 a 5, Change 3 a 2. History Value = 3 + 5 + 2 = 10. Higher means you've got a real record to learn from. Low or zero means you've been changing things without leaving a trail.
question: Write down the last big change you made to your business and what you expected it to do.
closing_statement: Untracked changes mean you can't learn from your own history.
